examples.question_text:
Write these mixed numbers as improper fractions.
(a) $4\frac{3}{7}$
(b) $-5\frac{2}{9}$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Each whole has seven sevenths. Four wholes have $4\times7=28$ sevenths; add the extra three sevenths.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4\frac{3}{7}\\&=\frac{4\times7+3}{7}\\&=\frac{31}{7}\end{aligned}$
(b) First convert the positive part.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5\frac{2}{9}\\&=\frac{5\times9+2}{9}\\&=\frac{47}{9}\end{aligned}$
Put the minus sign back: $-5\frac{2}{9}=-\frac{47}{9}$.

examples.question_text:
Write these improper fractions as whole or mixed numbers in simplest form.
(a) $\frac{29}{6}$
(b) $\frac{35}{10}$
(c) $\frac{72}{9}$

examples.solution_text:
(a) Make an equivalent fraction with denominator $100$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{23}{4}\\&=\frac{23\times25}{4\times25}\\&=\frac{575}{100}\\&=5.75\end{aligned}$
(b) First change the mixed number to an improper fraction.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\frac{5}{8}\\&=\frac{2\times8+5}{8}\\&=\frac{21}{8}\end{aligned}$
Now make the denominator $1000$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{21}{8}\\&=\frac{21\times125}{8\times125}\\&=\frac{2625}{1000}\\&=2.625\end{aligned}$

Each whole contains four quarters. The first grid shows four shaded quarters and the second shows three, giving seven quarters altogether.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1\frac{3}{4}\\&=\frac{4+3}{4}\\&=\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}$
